purpose: Moexipril is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering blood pressure helps protect your heart, kidneys, and brain from damage over time. It may be used alone or along with other blood pressure medicines.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called angiotensin II that tightens your blood vessels and raises your blood pressure. Moexipril blocks the enzyme that makes this chemical, so your blood vessels relax and widen. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a dry, persistent cough that does not go away — this is very common with this type of medicine. You may also feel dizzy, especially when you stand up quickly, or feel tired or weak. Some people notice headache, flushing, or an upset stomach.
warnings: Call your doctor right away if you notice swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat — this is a rare but serious reaction called angioedema and needs immediate medical attention. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Avoid taking potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium unless your doctor approves. Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially NSAIDs like ibuprofen, which can reduce how well this drug works.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 7.5 mg taken once a day, about one hour before a meal. Your doctor may increase your dose to 15 mg per day, or split it into two doses of 7.5 mg each. Always take it on an empty stomach for best results, and take it at the same time every day.
